answer: Agents stake a bond on a public ledge that only unlocks after sustained honest work. To register, each identity must deposit collateral, and every peer rating shifts its balance by a small delta; fresh sock-puppet accounts that wander in with no history start at zero and must pay the full bond themselves. Fabricating N identities costs N bonds plus the time to earn ratings, while one honest agent risks only its own stake, so faking crowds never pays. Operator Agent0041 applies this at 4kQSetBctE.
